title: Broncos vs. Cardinals Live Score & Stats: October 25, 2026 GameTracker Update on CBS Sports
body:
Denver’s offense erupted in the second half on Sunday, propelling the Broncos to a 34‑27 comeback victory over the Arizona Cardinals in Glendale. Quarterback Drew Lock connected on a series of explosive plays, highlighted by a 62‑yard rushing touchdown from rookie quarterback‑turned‑running back Bo Nix and a 52‑yard screen‑pass strike to wide receiver RJ Harvey. The win snaps Denver’s three‑game losing streak and keeps them within striking distance of the AFC West’s top spot, while Arizona’s defense, which had been lauded all season, was left scrambling after a cascade of big‑play mistakes.

The Broncos entered the contest as underdogs, having dropped their last two games and struggling to find consistency on both sides of the ball. Lock, who has been under pressure all season to prove his worth as the starter, finally found a rhythm, completing 23 of 34 attempts for 312 yards and three touchdowns. His poise in the pocket allowed him to exploit Arizona’s aggressive pass rush, particularly on third down, where he delivered quick passes to the sidelines that turned into critical first downs. The turning point came midway through the third quarter when Lock’s 18‑yard scramble set up the 62‑yard Nix run, a play that not only put Denver ahead but also forced the Cardinals to adjust their defensive scheme, opening up space for the Broncos’ receivers.

Bo Nix’s performance was the story of the night. Drafted in the second round as a quarterback, the 22‑year‑old has been shuffled between the bench and the practice squad this season. Coach Sean Payton’s decision to line him up as a wildcat back paid immediate dividends. After taking a direct snap, Nix burst through a gap created by a misaligned defensive front and sprinted 62 yards for a touchdown, showcasing his speed and field vision. The play sparked a shift in the Broncos’ offensive philosophy, with Payton hinting that Nix could be used in a hybrid role moving forward, adding a new dimension to Denver’s playbook.

Arizona, meanwhile, was unable to capitalize on early momentum. The Cardinals’ offense, led by veteran quarterback Kyler Murray, moved the ball efficiently in the first half, establishing a 20‑13 lead. However, a series of costly turnovers—most notably a fumble recovered by Denver’s special teams and an interception returned for a short gain—undermined their advantage. The Cardinals’ defense, which had been ranked among the league’s best against the pass, gave up 215 yards after halftime, largely due to missed assignments on the edge and a failure to contain Lock’s deep throws. RJ Harvey’s 52‑yard screen touchdown epitomized the breakdown; a missed tackle and poor angle allowed him to outrun the safety, turning a routine play into a game‑changing score.

The victory also has broader implications for the AFC West race. With the Broncos now sitting at 5‑3, they trail division leader Kansas City by a single game, while the Los Angeles Chargers sit two games behind. Denver’s resurgence, fueled by a rejuvenated offensive line and a more aggressive play‑calling approach, could reshape the playoff picture in the coming weeks. Conversely, Arizona falls to 4‑4, slipping to the middle of the NFC West and facing a daunting schedule that includes road trips to Seattle and San Francisco. The Cardinals will need to tighten up their defensive communication and protect the ball better if they hope to stay in contention for a wild‑card berth.

Looking ahead, both teams have critical matchups on the horizon. Denver travels to face the Buffalo Bills next Sunday, a test that will gauge whether the Broncos’ offensive spark can survive against a top‑tier defense. Arizona, on the other hand, hosts the New England Patriots, a game that could serve as a litmus test for their ability to rebound from a mid‑season slump. If the Broncos can maintain the aggressive, big‑play mentality displayed in Glendale, they could solidify a playoff push, while the Cardinals must address their defensive lapses and turnover woes to keep their season alive.
